source_platforms.name: ACN-Data (Caltech Adaptive Charging Network) - Lee, Li & Low, ACM e-Energy 2019
AgenticHEMS - Agentic AI Home Energy Management System: A Large Language Model Framework for Residential Load Scheduling (arXiv:2510.26603)

ground_truth_references: Minimum-cost feasible charging schedule computed by a real scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) solve at env reset (L4/envs/ev_v2g.py)
Per-van per-hour charging-power LP with departure-SoC, battery-capacity, EVSE-rating and per-hour site-limit (DR-reduced) constraints
Hard-constraint gating (all-vans-80%, <=120 kW, DR honored) + cost-vs-LP-optimum closeness, scored in [0,1]

agentic_tasks.prompt:
You are an autonomous EV fleet charging-management agent for a depot of 20 electric delivery vans. It is currently 17:00; all vans have just returned and plugged in. Your objectives, in priority order: (1) guarantee every van reaches at least 80% SOC by its 06:00 departure (HARD constraint), (2) keep total depot power within the 120 kW site limit at all times (HARD constraint), (3) respond to a demand-response event by reducing depot net power, and (4) minimize total energy cost.

Available tools:
- get_fleet_state(): returns each van's current SOC (%), battery capacity (kWh), and charger power (kW).
- get_price_forecast_24h(): returns 24 hourly prices ($/kWh).
- get_site_limit(): returns the depot power limit (kW).
- set_charge_schedule(van_id, start_hour, end_hour, power_kw): schedule a van's charging.
- get_dr_event(): returns any active demand-response event (window and requested reduction).
- respond_dr(event_id, reduction_kw): commit a depot-level power reduction during the event.
- log_decision(action, justification): record each decision with rationale.

Execute the workflow: inspect fleet and prices, compute each van's energy need, build a staggered charging plan that respects the 120 kW site limit and all departure deadlines, shift load to the cheapest hours, handle the DR event by curtailing/deferring flexible charging during its window, and log every decision. Finally report total cost, confirm all departure SOCs are met, and confirm the site limit and DR commitment were honored.

context.arrival_soc_note: Deterministic 25%-60% linear spread across vans 1-20 (mirrored exactly in L4/envs/ev_v2g.py for reproducibility). Total fleet energy need to reach 80% = sum((0.80 - soc)*60) = 450 kWh.
context.notes: If all 20 vans charged at 7.2 kW simultaneously that would be 144 kW, exceeding the 120 kW site limit, so charging MUST be staggered. The 13-hour 17:00->06:00 window (7 off-peak hours x 120 kW = 840 kWh capacity) easily covers the 450 kWh total need.

computed_optimum.method: scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS); per-van per-hour charging power, 0-7.2 kW; sum_h x[v,h] >= (0.80-soc_v)*60; sum_h x[v,h] <= (1-soc_v)*60; sum_v x[v,h] <= 120 kW per hour (60 kW during the 19:00-20:00 DR window)
computed_optimum.note: All 450 kWh placed at the $0.09 off-peak rate (450 * 0.09 = 40.50); reference peak concurrent power ~82 kW < 120 kW; zero charging in the DR window so the 60 kW DR commitment is free. Computed at env reset, never hardcoded as a grading constant.

reference_papers.citation: Z. J. Lee, T. Li, S. H. Low. ACN-Data: Analysis and Applications of an Open EV Charging Dataset. ACM e-Energy 2019.
reference_papers.role: Conceptual grounding for the managed-charging depot setting (Caltech Adaptive Charging Network studies exactly this site-limited deadline-charging problem). No ACN session data is consumed: arrival SoCs are a deterministic synthetic spread, disclosed in context.arrival_soc_note.

reference_papers.citation: W. Kempton, J. Tomic. Vehicle-to-grid power fundamentals: Calculating capacity and net revenue. Journal of Power Sources, 144(1), 2005.
reference_papers.role: Managed-charging fundamentals: per-vehicle energy, charger power bounds, aggregate site limits. Scope note: the episode is charging-only — the paper's bidirectional V2G export/net-revenue content is not exercised.

reference_papers.citation: R. El Makroum, S. Zwickl-Bernhard, L. Kranzl. Agentic AI Home Energy Management System: A Large Language Model Framework for Residential Load Scheduling (AgenticHEMS). arXiv:2510.26603, 2025.
reference_papers.role: Methodology basis for the single-shot agentic planning loop (perceive state -> reason about constraints -> emit verified tool-action schedule -> declare done), transferred from the home to the depot setting; same loop used by the sibling HEMS env vpp_scheduling_L4_002.

agentic_tasks.ground_truth: Correct agent behavior: (1) Calls get_fleet_state(), get_price_forecast_24h(), get_site_limit(), and get_dr_event() before scheduling. (2) Computes each van's energy need = (0.80 - arrival_soc) * 60 kWh (e.g., a van at 30% needs 30 kWh ~ 4.2 h at 7.2 kW); the deterministic 25%-60% spread gives a 450 kWh total fleet need. (3) Recognizes 20 x 7.2 = 144 kW > 120 kW site limit, so at most floor(120/7.2) = 16 vans can charge at full power simultaneously; staggers charging so concurrent power <= 120 kW. (4) Shifts the bulk of charging into off-peak hours (23:00 and 00:00-05:00 at $0.09) and away from the $0.30 peak hours 19-20. There is ample time: the 7-hour off-peak window covers the ~4-5 h each van needs. (5) Handles the DR event in hours 19-20 by NOT charging during that window to deliver the requested 60 kW reduction; since charging is best deferred to off-peak anyway, the agent commits respond_dr('DR-EV-2026-0182', 60) and schedules ~0 kW during 19-20. (6) Verifies every van reaches >= 80% by 06:00, the concurrent site power never exceeds 120 kW, and the DR reduction is honored. (7) Logs each decision with cost/constraint justification and reports a total cost equal to the 450 kWh fleet need priced entirely off-peak: the LP optimum is 450 * $0.09 = $40.50. Failure modes: exceeding the site limit, missing a departure SOC, or charging through the peak/DR window unnecessarily.
agentic_tasks.official_scoring_standard: Executable interactive scoring in [0,1], computed by L4/envs/ev_v2g.py::EVFleetDepotChargingEnv (loaded by eval/l4_runner.py). The episode is reset -> per-step JSON tool actions -> evaluate. HARD CONSTRAINTS are gating (0.60, equal thirds): (a) all 20 vans reach >= 80% SoC by 06:00 (the SoC third is graded on the fraction of vans that make it), (b) per-hour aggregate depot power <= 120 kW at every hour, (c) the 60 kW DR commitment is honored (committed >= 60 kW AND realized depot power during hours 19-20 stays at least the committed amount below the site limit). COST-OPTIMALITY (0.40): closeness of the realized energy cost to the LP reference optimum ($40.50, recomputed at reset via scipy.optimize.linprog, never a hardcoded grading constant), and discounted to 20% while any hard constraint is violated so a cheap-but-infeasible schedule cannot score high. A no-op / immediate declare_done scores low; a near-optimal feasible staggered schedule scores >= 0.9.
agentic_tasks.use_case: EV-grid integration & fleet-charging engineer managing smart & bidirectional EV/fleet charging against grid and battery limits — the autonomous operational decision loop the role (or a DERMS/agent acting for them) executes.
